sources.citation: Roger Blench West Chadic web directory (rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/Chadic/West/, the Internet Archive's index listing 2009-2024)
sources.note: Checked the archived directory tree: subfolders for Warji (Sirzakwai dictionary), Miya, Hausa, Ron, A3, B3 etc; no Kariya folder or Kariya wordlist/dictionary was ever posted.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1998. A Grammar of Miya. University of California Publications in Linguistics 130. Berkeley: UC Press (ch. 2-3 segmental and tonal phonology).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number Philol 346.20 vol. 130) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number Philol 346.20 vol. 130
sources.note: Full prosodic description of the closest well-described Warji-group relative (Miya, mkf; tonal analysis); useful as the group-level proxy if the catalog accepts sister-language evidence, but it is not a Kariya source.
No phonology; sole source cited is Blench 2012 draft.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Gobak, Fittokka; Danladi, Yakubu; Dabet, Julius; Riepe, Christina; Aregbesola, Adedamola; Abraham, Benard; Lewinan, Andrew; Araokanmi, Thelma. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. SIL International. 108 pp. (Internet Archive copy of sil.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 6.5 'Phonological comparison' is segmental correspondences only; Appendix G (p.64) on the Kariya/Tulu and other wordlists: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sec. 1.6 lists all prior work on Kariya: Temple 1922, Skinner 1977, Wente-Lukas 1985, Allsworth-Jones et al. 1986, Blench 1994/2012, Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994, CAPRO 1995, Haruna 2005 - none descriptive.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2012 [finalised draft, 8 Nov 2012]. Linguistic and cultural background to the North Bauchi region and the Wiihə people. Chapter prepared for P. Allsworth-Jones (ed.) 2015, Kariya Wuro: a Late Stone Age site in northern Nigeria, 93-104. Frankfurt am Main: Africa Magna. (Internet Archive copy of rogerblench.info/Archaeology/Africa/Background to the North Bauchi; live domain now squatted)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Overview of North Bauchi languages, quasi-reconstructions of cultural vocabulary from Skinner 1977, Wiihə history/clans/ritual; only prosodic remark is fn.1 'Tone-marks will not be given on all further citations of the name'.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena. (archive.org item SkinnerNorthBauchiChadic1977, text PDF + scanned txt)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' (AAL 4, p.5) gives a group-wide consonant/vowel inventory; on prosody only: 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' Nothing on stress/accent; Kariya ('K', Vinahe/Kariyanci, informant M. Usuman Sanusi) appears only as a column in the comparative wordlist.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. UCLA papers site (linguistics.ucla.edu/people/schuh/Papers/, the Internet Archive's index listing)
sources.note: Checked full archived file list: North Bauchi material is Miya only (1989a,b, 1998 grammar, 2001, 2010 dictionary); nothing on Kariya.
